recent_posts.title: Brave’s unique Shred button now available for Android, letting users enhance their privacy by easily discarding tracking site data
recent_posts.summary: Brave Browser version 1.89 brings the Shred button feature to Android, previously available only on iOS. The Shred button lets users instantly delete all data stored by a specific website — including cookies and local storage — without logging out of other sites. Users can trigger it manually from the tab switcher, contextual menu, or Shields panel, or configure Auto Shred to automatically clear site data when tabs are closed or the browser restarts. Auto Shred replaces the older 'forget me when I close this site' feature on Android, with existing preferences migrated automatically. Because Android has fewer platform restrictions than iOS, Brave can more thoroughly clean up first-party storage on Android.

recent_posts.title: Brave Search API approaches 700,000 OpenClaw users, highlighting the surge in machine-first search
recent_posts.summary: Brave Search API has reached nearly 700,000 users through OpenClaw, the leading open-source AI agent platform backed by OpenAI. Brave positions itself as the only viable independent search API alternative as Google limits access and Bing phases out its API. The post highlights the growing trend of machine-driven search, where AI agents require real-time web access at scale. Brave also claims its Ask Brave AI search (using open-weights Qwen3 and its LLM Context API) outperformed ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode in internal evaluations. A step-by-step guide is available for integrating Brave Search API with OpenClaw.

Brave Wallet now supports NEAR Intents
recent_posts.summary: Brave Wallet has integrated NEAR Intents in browser version v1.88, enabling cross-chain swaps across Bitcoin, Solana, Zcash, Cardano, and EVM chains without traditional bridges or manual gas handling. NEAR Intents uses intent-based transaction architecture to abstract cross-chain complexity, having already processed over 19 million swaps and $14 billion in volume across 35 chains. A notable feature is support for shielded Zcash transactions using zero-knowledge proofs, allowing private swaps with automatic return to the shielded pool on refunds.

recent_posts.title: Why Brave is opposing Google’s Android developer registry
recent_posts.summary: Brave has joined the EFF, Tor Project, and 40+ organizations opposing Google's plan to require all Android developers to register with government-issued ID starting September 2026, even those distributing apps outside the Play Store. The policy would create a centralized identity database of every Android developer, posing serious privacy risks especially for those building privacy tools, VPNs, and software for journalists and activists. Brave frames this as part of a broader pattern of Google leveraging platform control to insert itself into activities where users and developers didn't invite its involvement, alongside past moves like Manifest V2 deprecation, AMP, and Privacy Sandbox.

recent_posts.title: Privacy risks of agentic oversharing on the Web
recent_posts.summary: Research from Brave introduces SPILLAGE, a framework for measuring 'agentic oversharing' — the tendency of LLM-based web agents to inadvertently expose sensitive user data to third-party websites while completing tasks. Testing across Amazon and eBay with 1,080 runs using Browser-Use and AutoGen (backed by GPT-4o, O3, O4-mini) found oversharing is pervasive, with behavioral oversharing dominating content oversharing. Critically, prompt-level privacy instructions are insufficient to stop it. Counterintuitively, removing task-irrelevant data from agent inputs improved task success rates by up to 17.9%, showing privacy and utility are complementary rather than in conflict.

recent_posts.title: Brave Search API now features Place Search, a new endpoint for map applications
recent_posts.summary: Brave has launched Place Search, a new endpoint in the Brave Search API that enables geographic queries across 200+ million points of interest. Developers can search by center point, radius (up to 20km), and optional query string to find businesses, landmarks, and parks. Key features include granular location targeting, guaranteed location results (unlike regular search), roughly 2x faster response times, and an 'Explore Mode' for empty queries that surfaces popular nearby places. It's available to all Search plan subscribers with pay-as-you-go pricing and a free tier for small projects.

recent_posts.title: zkLogin: when ZKP is not enough
recent_posts.summary: Security researchers at Brave identified critical vulnerabilities in zkLogin, a zero-knowledge proof-based authorization system used in the Sui blockchain ecosystem. The analysis reveals three major vulnerability classes: ambiguous JWT parsing that allows claim shadowing and parser differentials, weak binding between authentication and authorization enabling cross-RP impersonation attacks, and centralization risks from outsourced proving services. The core issue is that zkLogin's security depends not just on cryptographic proofs, but on external assumptions about document correctness, issuer governance, and execution environments that the protocol doesn't enforce. The research demonstrates that repurposing short-lived OIDC tokens into long-lived authorization credentials without proper validation, canonical parsing, and cryptographic binding creates exploitable attack surfaces even when the underlying ZKP cryptography is sound.

recent_posts.title: Brave launches LLM Context API for AI applications
recent_posts.summary: Brave launched the LLM Context API, a search API optimized for AI applications that provides high-quality grounding data to LLMs. Internal testing shows that open-weight models using Brave's API data outperform ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode. The release includes simplified pricing ($5 per 1k requests for Search, $4 per 1k searches plus $5 per million tokens for Answers), developer tools including Skills and an API assistant, and features like Goggles for result filtering, token budget control, and zero data retention. Brave operates one of only three independent global-scale search indexes in the western world.

recent_posts.title: The Brave Search API’s integration into Snowflake enables agentic web search for enterprise customers
recent_posts.summary: Brave Search API is now integrated into Snowflake's AI tools (Cortex Code, Cortex Agents, and Snowflake Intelligence), enabling enterprise customers to perform real-time web searches within their AI applications. The integration bridges internal enterprise data with public web context, helping reduce AI hallucinations and improve accuracy. Brave Search API offers access to an independent index of 35+ billion pages with real-time updates, privacy-focused design, and SOC 2 Type II certification. It already powers most top 10 AI LLMs with web search data.

top_posts.title: Brave browser passes 100 million monthly active users
top_posts.summary: Brave browser reached 101 million monthly active users in September 2024, growing at 2.5 million users per month. Brave Search now handles 20 billion annualized queries with its independent index. The company has expanded into a privacy-focused ecosystem including Leo AI assistant, VPN services, and a cryptocurrency wallet, while building sustainable revenue through privacy-respecting ads, search API, and premium subscriptions. Brave emphasizes privacy-by-default design across all products, using aggregate analytics that don't collect personal user data.

top_posts.title: HTTPS by Default
top_posts.summary: Brave introduces the new feature 'HTTPS by Default' to improve web security and privacy by increasing the use of HTTPS. This feature automatically upgrades sites to HTTPS, falling back to HTTP only if necessary.

top_posts.title: Brave partners with Solana to integrate it into the browser and make it the default for DApp support
top_posts.summary: Brave will integrate the Solana blockchain into the Brave browser, providing default Solana ecosystem support to Brave’s 42 million monthly active users and 1.3 million verified Creators. Brave will soon default to Solana for cross-chain and Solana native DApps. Solana will also enable the implementation of the Themis protocol developed by Brave.
